Macron condemns “shocking” scenes of violence across France

Reuters

19 October, 2026 12:30 am IST

Follow Us :

PARIS, Oct 18 (Reuters) – French President Emmanuel Macron condemned on Sunday what he called the “dissenters” who looted and vandalised cities in “shocking” scenes across France on the sidelines of protests over the cost of living.

“Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: what was going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?” Macron said in a televised address to the nation. “Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame.”

Macron, whose final six months in office are being shaped by mounting political, fiscal and social pressures, said he had ordered a review to determine whether there had been failings in intelligence gathering or police preparedness before protests that were later marred by looting and violence.

Show Full Article

He said prefects and mayors would be empowered to ban certain gatherings where necessary.

Macron also said he had asked the government to bring together students, teachers, lawmakers, trade union representatives and business leaders this week to formulate what he described as “concrete proposals” to address the crisis, without providing further details.

“We must sit around the table and build solutions together,” he said.

(Reporting by Michel Rose and Sybille de La Hamaide; editing by Richard Lough)

Milan police clash with protesters on second day of unrest

Reuters

18 October, 2026 11:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MILAN, Oct 18 (Reuters) – Milan police clashed on Sunday with protesters throwing stones and looting shops during demonstrations against poor services and the rising cost of living, a day after similar unrest in several Italian cities.

Police in riot gear fired tear gas and used water cannons after several hundred hooded protesters broke shop windows and set bins on fire in the area near central Piazza Duomo, sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters.

More than 60 protesters were taken to the police station for further checks, the sources added.

Show Full Article

A total of 28 protesters were arrested after similar clashes erupted on Saturday in northern cities including Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, according to a police report on Sunday.

The clashes had echoes of the violence in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country’s most violent protests in years.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, facing an election next year, condemned the violence and announced a government meeting on Monday to discuss how to address the situation.

(Reporting by Sara Rossi; Editing by Jan Harvey)

Lithuanians forced to take shelter after suspected drone enters airspace

Reuters

18 October, 2026 08:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Andrius Sytas VILNIUS, Oct 18 (Reuters) – A suspected drone exploded over Lithuania after triggering an alert that forced residents in northern and central areas to seek shelter for an hour on Sunday morning, the president and other defence officials said.

Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said later it regretted the incident in Lithuania’s airspace, adding that it may have resulted from Russian electronic warfare diverting drones off course.

The object flew into Lithuania’s airspace from Poland, Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas told reporters, after proposing a joint investigation to his Polish counterpart.

Show Full Article

“Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is spilling over onto the Eastern flank of NATO and EU,” Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda said on X.

“What appears to be a drone exploded over the northern part of the country, posing a danger to the civilian population,” he added.

NATO SCRAMBLES FIGHTERS

Poland’s military said it was also verifying a possible violation of its airspace by an unidentified object.

A Polish Defence Ministry spokesperson later said radar systems did not confirm the object crossing the border into Lithuania, but added that Polish authorities were remaining in contact with Lithuanian officials.

During the “red” alert, NATO fighter jets were scrambled to the area, and Kaunas airport, near Lithuania’s second-largest city, was temporarily closed, the Lithuanian government’s crisis management centre said.

The NATO aircraft were unable to visually identify the object due to cloudy weather and did not attempt to shoot it down, the centre said.

Lithuanian army personnel were investigating possible drone debris near Juodzionys village in northern Lithuania, after the object disappeared from radar, possibly after exploding, the centre said.

Some of the debris struck a civilian vehicle, Kaunas said.

“We can confirm that two Italian Eurofighter jets were scrambled earlier today in response to a drone over Lithuanian airspace,” a NATO official said.

“The aircraft were operating under NATO command. An investigation is ongoing, and NATO remains in close contact with the Lithuanian authorities,” the official said, adding that the alliance was ready and able to react to any potential threat.

Northern neighbour Latvia briefly issued a “yellow” air warning in some regions bordering Lithuania, citing a “possible threat”, its army said.

Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered NATO airspace in the Baltic region in recent months. Kyiv has said they were steered off course by Russian signal jamming.

This has stoked concerns that Russia’s war in Ukraine is spilling over NATO’s borders.

(Reporting by Andrius Sytas in Vilnius; Additional reporting by Lili Bayer in Brussels and Anna Koper in Warsaw; Editing by Saad Sayeed, William Mallard, Elaine Hardcastle and Joe Bavier)
